title: Human-factors security requirements (machine-checked)
intro: Each requirement below is backed by Tamarin proofs over the ceremony-mask model. A 'risk' lemma (exists-trace) shows the unsafe human outcome is REACHABLE; a 'removed_by' lemma (all-traces) shows a named lever makes it UNREACHABLE. The requirement is the normative consequence of that proof pair.

requirements.title: Low-effort fingerprint comparison
requirements.risk_text: A raw hex key-fingerprint comparison is high-Effort (NASA-TLX), which triggers the Abstraction stressor: the user stops reasoning (Naive) and accepts a tampered key (a Mistake) -> the secret is encrypted to the adversary.

removed_by.lever: presenting the comparison via a low-effort affordance (a side-by-side visual diff), which keeps the user Attentive

requirements.requirement: Implementations MUST present key-fingerprint comparison via a low-effort affordance (e.g. a side-by-side visual diff or word-list), not a raw hexadecimal string.

requirements.title: Engaged-user value on approval prompts (number matching)
requirements.risk_text: A habituated user (repeated prompts) OR a user under adversary-induced urgency reflexively auto-approves a prompt of any kind, including an adversary-injected one (MFA prompt-bombing / fatigue).

removed_by.lever: requiring an engaged-user value (number matching) the reflexive user cannot supply

requirements.requirement: Implementations MUST require an engaged-user value (e.g. number matching) on security-critical approval prompts, so that a habituated or time-pressured user cannot approve an adversary-injected prompt.

requirements.title: Detect-and-halt key confirmation
requirements.risk_text: A user under high cognitive load / time pressure slips and computes a wrong key; without a check, the ceremony completes with the wrong key (unsafe success).

removed_by.lever: a key-confirmation step that detects the mismatch and halts

requirements.requirement: Implementations MUST verify the derived/agreed key against an expected value and halt on mismatch, so that a slip cannot complete the ceremony with a wrong key.

requirements.title: Automatic (device-side) fingerprint comparison
requirements.risk_text: Leaving the fingerprint comparison to the user's mental model lets a Naive user accept a tampered fingerprint.

removed_by.lever: the device comparing the fingerprints automatically and refusing a tampered one

requirements.requirement: Implementations SHOULD compare security-critical fingerprints automatically (device-side) rather than relying on the user, so a tampered fingerprint cannot be accepted.

requirements.title: Out-of-band secret channel
requirements.risk_text: Sending a sharing password in-band (same channel as the ciphertext) lets the adversary decrypt; a Careless user takes that shortcut and leaks it silently.

removed_by.lever: sending the password over a channel OTHER than the message (with no degraded share, secrecy is absolute)

requirements.requirement: Implementations MUST transmit a sharing password/secret over a channel other than the protected message itself.

requirements.title: Cover the least-skilled intended population
requirements.risk_text: A step that is low-demand for an expert can be high-demand (overwhelming) for a novice, who then slips. A ceremony proven safe for experts may be unsafe for novices.

removed_by.lever: the expert population (low demand) -- which a novice does NOT enjoy; so the safety is population-scoped

requirements.requirement: The analysis/deployment MUST consider the least-skilled intended user population (the slip is reachable for novices though not experts); equivalently, the interface MUST lower the step's demand for everyone.

requirements.title: Disable the send control until verification completes
requirements.risk_text: When the composer shows the Send button CO-PRESENT with the unfinished key verification, a degraded user can authorise the send BEFORE the fingerprint has been checked at all. This is not a wrong answer to a prompt -- it is answering the prompts OUT OF ORDER, and the resulting message leaves the boundary unverified. The old model could not even express this: a ceremony whose steps are joined linearly cannot produce an out-of-order trace.

removed_by.lever: a forcing function: the Send control is disabled (not merely warned about) until the recipient's key has been verified, so the out-of-order grant has no route to the wire

requirements.requirement: Implementations MUST disable the send action until recipient-key verification has completed. A warning or a confirmation dialog is NOT sufficient: the degraded user grants it.

requirements.title: Disable session start until key confirmation completes (second ceremony)
requirements.risk_text: The SAME order violation appears in a completely different ceremony: in the manual key-establishment messenger, a degraded user presses 'start session' before the key read-back, and the session goes live on an unconfirmed -- possibly slipped or substituted -- key. The shutdown that would have caught it is simply skipped.

removed_by.lever: the same forcing function: 'start session' is disabled until the key confirmation read-back has completed

requirements.requirement: Implementations MUST disable session establishment until key confirmation has completed. This is the SAME requirement as REQ-VERIFY-BEFORE-SEND, proved necessary in a second, independent ceremony -- which is what makes it a general design rule rather than an artefact of one protocol.

requirements.title: No silent plaintext fallback in the encryption selector
requirements.risk_text: When the encryption selector offers 'Standard (TLS only)' alongside the protected methods, a degraded user picks the wrong route and the message is handed to the provider in the clear. Nothing about the send looks unusual to the user.

removed_by.lever: removing the plaintext exit from the selector for a correspondent whose key is available (the composer's per-recipient lock indicator already knows this)

requirements.requirement: Implementations MUST NOT offer an unprotected send route as a peer option in the encryption selector when a protected route is available for the recipient.

requirements.title: Forward must re-encrypt or block
requirements.risk_text: The recipient-side breach: every SENDER step can be perfect and the message still leaves the boundary, because a degraded recipient forwards it to a third party for whom no key exists and the client silently sends it in the clear. This is a breach of 'only the correspondents know m' that no sender-side mitigation can prevent.

removed_by.lever: Forward re-encrypts to the new recipient or BLOCKS -- it never silently downgrades to cleartext

requirements.requirement: Implementations MUST NOT silently downgrade a forwarded protected message to cleartext. Forward MUST either re-protect for the new recipient or refuse.
